legend: It is well known that Alan is a great mathematics enthusiast and he enjoys learning about mathematics facts. Recently, he read about a fact related to the first digit of numbers: the Benford's law, also known as the first-digit law. This law states that, in many collections of numbers from the real life, the most frequent first-digit is 1$$$1$$$. Moreover, it also states that the small digits are more likely to be the first-digits than the greater digits.

Alan read that the law is satisfied in many collections of numbers, such as river lengths, mountain heights, country populations, prices, people ages, house numbers, etc. In all of these collections, the digit 1$$$1$$$ is the most likely to be the first digit. Fascinated with this fact, Alan decided to make his own experiment and see if Benford's law is satisfied.

Before beginning with the experiment, Alan put N$$$N$$$ buckets in a line and prepared K$$$K$$$ balls. The experiment consists of K$$$K$$$ steps. During the i$$$i$$$-th step, he selects a bucket randomly and inserts the i$$$i$$$-th ball in that bucket. The selection of the bucket is independent across each step and all buckets have the same probability of being selected.

Once all steps are finished, Alan will count the number of balls in each bucket and write the results in a list L$$$L$$$. Let cd$$$c_d$$$ be the number of elements in L$$$L$$$ which has d$$$d$$$ as the first-digit, Alan wants to check if c1$$$c_1$$$ is the greater across all cd$$$c_d$$$ to see if Benford's law is satisfied (spoiler: for large values of N$$$N$$$, Benford's law is satisfied in this experiment).

But when there was M$$$M$$$ steps left to finish the experiment, Alan got tired of selecting buckets and inserting balls. So, he decided to ask you for help to finish his experiment. Given the number of balls in each bucket so far, what is the expected value of c1,c2,…,c9$$$c_1, c_2, \dots, c_9$$$ after performing the remaining M$$$M$$$ steps?
input: The first line contains two integers N$$$N$$$ and M$$$M$$$ (1≤N≤105$$$1 \leq N \leq 10^5$$$ and 0≤M≤105$$$0 \leq M \leq 10^5$$$), the number of buckets in the experiment and the number of remaining steps.
The second line contains N$$$N$$$ characters a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ (0≤ai≤105$$$0 \leq a_i \leq 10^5$$$), where ai$$$a_i$$$ is the number of ball in the i$$$i$$$-th bucket so far.
output: Print 9$$$9$$$ lines. In the i$$$i$$$-th line, print the expected value of ci$$$c_i$$$. We can show that the expected value can be represented in the form pq$$$\frac{p}{q}$$$, where q≠0$$$q \neq 0$$$ and gcd(p,q)=1$$$gcd(p,q) = 1$$$. Print the expected value as p∗q−1$$$p*q^{-1}$$$ modulo 998244353$$$998244353$$$.

legend.ai: 众所周知，Alan 是一位数学爱好者，他喜欢了解数学事实。最近，他读到了一个与数字的首位有关的事实：本福特定律，也称为首位数字定律。该定律指出，在现实生活中的许多数字集合中，最常出现的首位数字是 1$$$1$$$。此外，该定律还指出，较小的数字比更大的数字更有可能作为首位数字。
Alan 了解到，在许多数字集合中都满足这一规律，例如河流长度、山脉高度、国家人口、价格、人的年龄、门牌号等。在所有这些集合中，数字 1$$$1$$$ 最有可能作为首位数字。Alan 对这一事实十分着迷，于是决定进行自己的实验，看看是否满足本福特定律。
在开始实验之前，Alan 将 N$$$N$$$ 个桶排成一列，并准备了 K$$$K$$$ 个球。实验由 K$$$K$$$ 个步骤组成。在第 i$$$i$$$ 步中，他随机选择一个桶，并将第 i$$$i$$$ 个球放入该桶中。每一步中桶的选择相互独立，并且每个桶被选中的概率都相同。
所有步骤完成后，Alan 将统计每个桶中的球数，并将结果写入列表 L$$$L$$$。设 cd$$$c_d$$$ 为 L$$$L$$$ 中首位数字为 d$$$d$$$ 的元素数量，Alan 想检查 c1$$$c_1$$$ 是否在所有 cd$$$c_d$$$ 中最大，以判断是否满足本福特定律(剧透：当 N$$$N$$$ 较大时，本福特定律在该实验中确实成立)。
但是，当还剩 M$$$M$$$ 步就能完成实验时，Alan 厌倦了选择桶并放入球。因此，他决定请求你的帮助来完成实验。给定目前每个桶中的球数，执行剩余的 M$$$M$$$ 步后，c1,c2,…,c9$$$c_1, c_2, \dots, c_9$$$ 的期望值是多少？

input.ai: 第一行包含两个整数 N$$$N$$$ 和 M$$$M$$$(1≤N≤105$$$1 \leq N \leq 10^5$$$ 且 0≤M≤105$$$0 \leq M \leq 10^5$$$)，分别表示实验中的桶数和剩余步数。
第二行包含 N$$$N$$$ 个字符 a1,a2,…,an$$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$(0≤ai≤105$$$0 \leq a_i \leq 10^5$$$)，其中 ai$$$a_i$$$ 表示目前第 i$$$i$$$ 个桶中的球数。

output.ai: 输出 9$$$9$$$ 行。在第 i$$$i$$$ 行中，输出 ci$$$c_i$$$ 的期望值。可以证明，该期望值可以表示为 pq$$$\frac{p}{q}$$$ 的形式，其中 q≠0$$$q \neq 0$$$ 且 gcd(p,q)=1$$$gcd(p,q) = 1$$$。输出 p∗q−1$$$p*q^{-1}$$$ 对 998244353$$$998244353$$$ 取模后的结果。
